name: Mental Maths: 3-Digit Subtraction
description: A KaTeX-enabled mental-arithmetic deck for subtracting three-digit numbers. It teaches left-to-right chunking, regrouping as place-value trading, multiple boundary crossings, across-zero subtraction, compensation, counting up, complements to 100/500/1000, estimation, error detection, and strategy selection.
estimatedTime: 130–170 minutes for the first pass; then 10–15 minute mixed review sessions

cards.term: 3-Digit Subtraction: What is the safest default mental method?
cards.definition:
Subtract the hundreds, tens, and ones of the smaller number from left to right.

$$
\begin{aligned}
764-238 \\
&=764-200-30-8 \\
&=564-30-8 \\
&=526
\end{aligned}
$$
This avoids holding a long written-borrowing procedure in your head.

cards.term: 3-Digit Subtraction: Why is left-to-right subtraction useful?
cards.definition:
It keeps a meaningful running total.

$$
\begin{aligned}
683-247 \\
&=683-200=483 \\
&=483-40=443 \\
&=443-7=436
\end{aligned}
$$
Each step is simple and easy to self-check.

Regrouping means exchanging one larger place-value unit for ten smaller ones.

For example,
523 = 400 + 110 + 13.

So:
$$
\begin{aligned}
523-178 \\
&=(400+110+13)-(100+70+8) \\
&=300+40+5 \\
&=345
\end{aligned}
$$
It is a place-value trade, not a memorised trick.

cards.term: 3-Digit Subtraction: When should you use compensation?
cards.definition:
Use compensation when the number being subtracted is close to a friendly 100, 500, or 1000.

$$
\begin{aligned}
684-297 \\
&=684-300+3 \\
&=387
\end{aligned}
$$
The correction is small, so this is easier than ordinary subtraction.

cards.term: 3-Digit Subtraction: When is counting up better?
cards.definition:
Count up when the two numbers are close or when the smaller number is near a clean hundred.

$$
\begin{aligned}
503-487 \\
487\to500 &= 13 \\
500\to503 &= 3 \\
503-487 &= 16
\end{aligned}
$$
You are finding the distance, not taking away in columns.

cards.term: 3-Digit Subtraction: How do you subtract from a round hundred?
cards.definition:
Break one hundred into tens and ones only when needed, or subtract in chunks.

$$
\begin{aligned}
700-468 \\
&=700-400-60-8 \\
&=300-60-8 \\
&=232
\end{aligned}
$$
The chunking route avoids confusing chains of borrowing.

cards.term: 3-Digit Subtraction: How do you subtract from 1000 mentally?
cards.definition:
Think in complements: find what must be added to the subtrahend to make 1000.

$$
\begin{aligned}
1000-248 &= 752 \\
248+752 &= 1000
\end{aligned}
$$
This is especially useful for numbers near 1000.

First subtract enough to reach a friendly hundred, then subtract the remainder.

$$
\begin{aligned}
543-178 \\
&=543-43-135 \\
&=500-135 \\
&=365
\end{aligned}
$$
Use it when the starting number is close to a lower hundred.

cards.term: 3-Digit Subtraction: When should you not force a shortcut?
cards.definition:
Use straight left-to-right chunking when no friendly base gives a clear advantage.

For 756 − 234, simply do:
$$
\begin{aligned}
756-234 \\
&=756-200-30-4 \\
&=522
\end{aligned}
$$
Fast mental maths means using the least demanding accurate route.

cards.term: 3-Digit Subtraction: How do you estimate a 3-digit difference?
cards.definition:
Round each number to a nearby hundred, then compare your exact answer with the estimate.

Example:
684 − 297 ≈ 700 − 300 = 400.

The exact answer 387 is reasonable; an answer near 300 is suspicious.

cards.term: 3-Digit Subtraction: What is a complement to 500?
cards.definition:
A complement to 500 is the number that must be added to a given number to make 500.

Example:
187 + 313 = 500, so 500 − 187 = 313.

Friendly totals such as 100, 500, and 1000 reduce mental workload.

cards.term: 3-Digit Subtraction: Which method is best for 503 − 487?
cards.definition:
Counting up.

$$
\begin{aligned}
487\to500 &=13 \\
500\to503 &=3 \\
503-487 &=16
\end{aligned}
$$
The gap is small and 500 is an effortless bridge.

cards.term: 3-Digit Subtraction: Which method is best for 684 − 297?
cards.definition:
Compensation to 300.

$$
\begin{aligned}
684-297 \\
&=684-300+3 \\
&=387
\end{aligned}
$$
The correction is only 3.

cards.term: 3-Digit Subtraction: Which method is best for 1000 − 648?
cards.definition:
Complement to 1000.

648 + 352 = 1000, so 1000 − 648 = 352.

This is cleaner than a chain of borrows across zeros.

753 − 201 = 753 − 200 − 1.
